short: Tensile deformation behavior and mechanical properties of a
title: Tensile deformation behavior and mechanical properties of a bulk cast Al0.9CoFeNi2 eutectic high-entropy alloy

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Structural high-entropy alloys need strength and tensile ductility at once, and a castable bulk route rather than a laboratory arc-melted button. How the two eutectic phases divide the deformation, and how their dislocation substructures evolve with strain, has not been followed in a Cr-free eutectic HEA.
states.detail: Absorbed: f1 (HYP/need), f2 (HYP/gap), f3 (HYP/hypothesis), f4 (DES/base_system), f5 (DES/method), f6 (PRC/forming), f7 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: The AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA has the same FCC (L12) plus B2 dual-phase lamellar structure

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The as-cast alloy is a dual-phase ordered FCC (L12) plus ordered BCC (B2) structure. A full eutectic cell morphology: a flat coarse band through the cell centre surrounded by regular two-phase lamellae 1-2 um wide.
states.detail: Absorbed: f8 (STR/phase/identity), f9 (STR/microstructure/shape), f12 (STR/defect/extended), f13 (STR/defect/extended), f14 (STR/defect/extended)

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Yield strength 559 MPa, ultimate tensile strength 1005 MPa and 6.2% tensile elongation at room temperature. Work hardening runs in three stages and adds 446 MPa between yield and ultimate strength, which delays necking.
states.detail: Absorbed: f15 (PRP/value), f16 (PRP/value), f17 (PRP/behavior_class), f18 (MEC/pathway), f19 (MEC/pathway). Premises: The ordered FCC (L12) phase is the soft, ductile constituent and the B2 phase the hard, brittle one; Dislocations banked against a boundary generate a back stress that raises the stress needed for further slip; Planar dislocation configurations such as slip bands and coplanar arrays indicate a low stacking-fault energy and difficult cross slip

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: A bulk-cast Cr-free eutectic HEA reaches 1005 MPa with 6.2% elongation because its two lamellar phases yield in sequence and the soft phase hardens steadily

nodes.title: TEM, F3, F5
nodes.head: One lamella is filled edge to edge with dense mottled dislocation contrast while the lamellae above and below it are featureless. Two circled dislocation outcrops sit on a field of mottled contrast crossed by faint linear traces.
nodes.solves: At 0.6% strain dislocations appear only in the FCC lamellae and bank up at the FCC/B2 boundaries; the B2 stays free of them
nodes.note: a discrete pile-up array is not resolvable in this mottled contrast; what the panel shows is that the contrast stops at the lamella boundary the text describes a single straight, parallel set; the panel shows two crossing families

nodes.title: TEM, F4
nodes.head: Dark dislocation tangles line the lamella boundaries, a dark band runs along one lamella, and the interiors carry cell walls and intersecting dislocation lines
nodes.solves: At 1.5% the FCC dislocation density is much higher and carries slip bands, boundary pile-ups, intersections and networks; the B2 is still free
nodes.note: the in-panel labels read 'Dislocations pileup' on both (a) and (c), while the caption calls (a) 'dislocation configurations' and only (c) a pileup
nodes.necessity_reason: S1 keeps shown support from g2, g4, g12, g14 after removal.

nodes.title: TEM, F5
nodes.head: The two post-fracture panels are taken at 0.5 um and 0.2 um scale bars, so the claim that the FCC dislocation density exceeds the B2 one cannot be read from this pair
nodes.solves: After fracture the FCC holds dense Taylor lattices and dislocation walls, and straight dislocations have finally appeared in the B2 as well

nodes.title: SEM, F2
nodes.head: The fracture surface is a mosaic of fan-shaped lamellar facets separated by raised tear ridges, with small voids strung along the lamellae
nodes.solves: Fracture is mixed: ductile tearing along the FCC lamellae with flat brittle-like facets on the B2 lamellae and voids on the phase boundaries
nodes.note: the red squares, red arrows, chevrons and blue circle drawn on the high-magnification panel are not explained in the caption, so which features belong to the B2 phase cannot be read off the panel
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and S2 keeps shown support from g6, g11.

nodes.title: TEM, F4
nodes.head: The lamella interiors are filled with curved, tangled cell walls rather than the straight coplanar arrays that define planar slip
nodes.solves: Accumulating bands, networks and walls in the FCC hold the hardening rate up through stage II; when the boundary stress reaches the B2 yield strength the B2 gives way and stage III begins
nodes.note: cell-like walls are the signature of wavy slip and easy cross slip, which cuts against the paper's low stacking-fault-energy, difficult-cross-slip reading of the same panels

use: The microstructures of the $\mathsf { A l } _ { 0 . 9 } \mathsf { C o F e N i } _ { 2 }$ EHEA are confirmed by the EBSD phase mapping and TEM-SAED (select area electron-beam diffraction) patterns, and the results are given in Fig. 1(b–e), respectively.
Fig. 1(c–e) shows the TEM micrograph and the SAED patterns of the as-cast alloy.

At an initial deformation of $0 . 6 \%$ , a number of dislocations occur in the soft FCC $\left( \mathrm { L } 1 _ { 2 } \right)$ phase, while no obvious dislocations are observed in the hard/brittle B2 phase (see Fig. 3(a)).

10.1016/j.jmst.2020.05.053#F3b.definition: dislocations configurations in the FCC $\left( \operatorname { L } 1 _ { 2 } \right)$ ) phase
use: As presented in Fig. 3(b), the FCC $\left( \operatorname { L } 1 _ { 2 } \right)$ phase exhibited obvious planar deformation characteristics, such as the dislocation planar slip and dislocation outcrop (marked with a red circle).

10.1016/j.jmst.2020.05.053#F5a.definition: dislocations configurations in the FCC $\left( \mathrm { L } 1 _ { 2 } \right)$ ) phase
use: As shown in Fig. 5(a), the FCC $\left( \operatorname { L } 1 _ { 2 } \right)$ phase exhibits a dense dislocation network arrangement formed by typical Taylor lattices, in which the parallel dislocation configuration is called the dislocation wall.
At the same time, grain boundaries are known to constitute strong obstacles to the dislocation motion, resulting in the formation of dislocation pile-ups (denoted by the arrow in Fig. 5(a)).

10.1016/j.jmst.2020.05.053#F5b.definition: dislocations configurations in the B2 phase
use: Thus, the straight and parallel dislocation morphology can be seen in the B2 phase at this deformation level, as shown in Fig. 5(b).

10.1016/j.jmst.2020.05.053#F4a.definition: dislocations configurations in the FCC $\left( \operatorname { L } 1 _ { 2 } \right)$ phase
use: As the deformation amount increases to ${ \sim } 1 . 5 \%$ , still no obvious dislocation are observed in the hard/brittle B2 phase, while the dislocations density is significantly increased in the FCC $\left( \operatorname { L } 1 _ { 2 } \right)$ phase (shown in Fig. 4(a)).

Meanwhile, some planar dislocation configurations, for instance, dislocation slip band (shown in Fig. 4(b)), dislocation build-up (presented in Fig. 4(c)), dislocation intersection (exhibited in Fig. 4(d)) dislocation networks (represented in Fig. 4(e)) are observed in the FCC $\left( \operatorname { L } 1 _ { 2 } \right)$ phase.

From Fig. 1(b), the $\mathsf { A l } _ { 0 . 9 } \mathsf { C o F e N i } _ { 2 }$ EHEA exhibits a full eutectic cell morphology.

In order to understand the excellent mechanical properties of the $\mathsf { A l } _ { 0 . 9 } \mathsf { C o F e N i } _ { 2 }$ EHEA, the fracture surface was observed by SEM (as shown in Fig. 2(c) and (d)).

From Fig. 2(c), the fracture surface is mainly composed of the ductility tear edge and elongated groove microstructure, which is similar to the $\mathsf { A l C o C r F e N i } _ { 2 . 1 }$ EHEA [25].
